 # Product Support Agent #
 This repository contains a small AI-enabled application that demonstrates architecture judgment, secure production thinking, hands-on engineering depth, and the ability to move from prototype to an operable solution.
 
 ## Goal ##
 
 The Goals is to use the following URLs which contains the Product list page and the search results API page as the sources and to design and build a working AI agent (select any model) to answer questions about supported products and their resources. 
 
 1. URLs https://my.opentext.com/support/products/ and API https://my.opentext.com/api/web/support/search-results?start=1&maxResults=5&text=*. If none of these works then load from the feed https://my.opentext.com/api/web/feed/product. For each product there is a page hosted under https://my.opentext.com/support/products/{ProductCode} location where ProductCode is the "slug" property of the feed data. Each of the product support page contains knowledge articles and supporting documentations, retrieve the details from those documenation unless they are protected by authentication.
 
 2. Future requirement is to expand the agentic capability to the full support and service management system (OpenText Service Management). 
 
 3. Produce a concise architecture showing application components, identity and access, data flow, model interaction, trust boundaries, deployment, monitoring, and support ownership. 
 
 4. Document architecture decisions, security and privacy considerations, assumptions, risks, trade-offs, production-readiness gaps, and a phased path from proof of concept to production.
 
 ## Architecture Considerations ##
 
 1. I as a Senior AI Solution Architect is looking for a decoupled ingestion, Retrieval Tooling and Agentic Orchestration Architecture that would retrieve/ fetch the product listing and queries the search API with controlled pagination. It would honor the HTTP response types and act accordinlgy, as an example, if the status code is HTTP 401 then it would avoid loading the page since this demonstration should work with anonymous access alone. OpenText has multiple product knowlede/ documentations which are protected by Customer Authorization, I would skil thopse records entrirely after recording at a central place about the reason. The ingestion should run through a queue, where the entries would be loaded from the Product list, each queue item would store only one product detail, and the ingestion worker would take one item from the queue, fetch the relevant details from the supporting URLs, run the details through embedding and store it in the knowledge source. It should record the details about the operation, especially whether it is a success or failure. For this MVP I would like to select 100 products randomly from the Product list and have only those 100 ingested. I will keep the list of 100 selected product so that I can surface the names to the chat agent which will be used by the endusers during the demonstration. I would clearly indicate that this is a demo process and only the list of 100 products got ingested to avoid requiring additional infrastructure and also to avoid putting load on OpenText's infrastructure.
 2. If the product list is empty then the ingestion and normalization process would terminate. If there is a rate limitation with HTTP 429 status code then I would check for suggested retry time and perform exponential backoff before retrying.
 3. The ingestion process should normalize the results into a canonical document schema for idempotent operations and delta updates for subsequent runs.
 4. I need a hybrid search implementaion since the endusers could search with keyword/ metadata and also through semantic meanings
 5. I would keep the source URLs so that I can present the actual URL with the search results in the agent.
 6. For the agent and orchestration layer I will use an LLM with structured tool/ function calling plus retrieval augmented generation (RAG)
 7. I would enforce strict context grounding, prompt injection related defense and PII/SPI/secret redaction from logs.
 8. I don't want to show the past search histories to the enduser in this MVP but I would retail all the logs/ traces/ queries/ responses from all user sessions so that those can be reviewed later to improve the experience and detect malicious attempts.
 9. I would keep the embedding and a chat completion model behind a gateway so that I can change the models in the future without changing the code.
 10. I need every claim about a supported product or resource to map back to a retrieved source URL/ID and do not want the model to invent links or resource ever.
 11. I need to include OpenTelemetry based AI request tracing, logging and metrics, which would be sent to any capable product like Aspire or Arize Phoenix.
 12. I need an offline evaluation dataset to test factual grounding, citation accuracy etc.
 13. I would include AI Gateway, managed identity based authentication, automated build, deployment, code quality analysis, SAST, DAST and IAST validations.
 14. I also need to prepare a phased path to take this proof of concept demonstration to Production where real users can use it. This will have usability, accessibility etc. validations to ensure that I am building a product what will be helpful to the endusers and not just a working prototype that works but not useful for anyone.
 15. For each of the phases I want end to end testability. Each of the steps should be testable independently and completion of a phase require successful execution of the relevant test cases. I want unit test, integration test, end to end test etc.
 16. I want to ensure that the project repository has proper structure so that it's easily readable and understandable by my other colleagues. All architectural decisions are logged, appropriate architecture documentations are created with architecture diagrams created in mermaid syntax.
 17. Use a TypeScript React/Next.js frontend for the user-facing chat interface and a Python FastAPI backend. Build agents in Python with Microsoft Agent Framework. Use MongoDB locally and Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB in the cloud. Use the user-provided Azure AI Search service for both local and cloud search; do not add a local vector store. Use LiteLLM locally and Azure API Management in the cloud as model gateways. Use system-assigned managed identity for cloud application access where supported, and Azure Key Vault for cloud secrets. Defer caching unless measurements justify it. Use Azurite locally and Azure Storage Queue in the cloud. Use Podman for local development.
 18. I need to create a infrastructure deployment pipeline based on Bicep, which will have infrastructure as code scripts for the entire cloud infrastructure. This will include a Azure Virtual Network, Azure APIM will be deployed in external mode with VENT integration. All the backed services, agents, data store, queue etc. will be under the VENT with appropriate subnets. I will need Log Analytics workspace and Azure Monitor for the logs/ metrics and traces.
 19. I will need a code build pipeline for the UI, backend API, AI Agents
 20. I will need a code deployment pipeline for the UI, backend API and AI Agents
 21. To host the backend use Azure Container Apps.
 22. Use GitHub Actions for the build and deployment pipelines

 # Product Support Agent
 
 This repository contains a review-gated, local-first product support assistant.
 The approved foundation uses a TypeScript React/Next.js frontend and a Python
 FastAPI backend. Phase 2 adds bounded catalog discovery, reproducible manifest
 selection, Azure Storage Queue-compatible product references, ingestion status,
 and a poison queue contract. Live source verification and live model use remain
 gated until their approved phase checks.
 
 See the [implementation plan](docs/implementation-plan.md) for phase gates and
 the [local development guide](docs/operations/local-development.md) for setup
 and validation commands.

 title: Product Support Agent Implementation Plan
 description: Review-gated implementation plan for a local-first product-support AI agent with a conceptual, statically validated Azure design in Canada Central
 author: Product Support Agent Team
 ms.date: 2026-11-21
 ms.topic: concept
 keywords:
   - product support
   - AI agent
   - architecture
   - implementation plan
 estimated_reading_time: 12
 ---
 
 ## Purpose and approval model
 
 This plan turns the requirements in [Instructions.md](../Instructions.md) into a staged, testable delivery path. Phase 0, Phase 0b, and Phase 1 have been approved; implementation is limited to the current approved phase. No cloud resources or application deployments are authorized.
 
 Each phase is a separate review gate. We will not begin a phase until you approve its scope, decisions, and exit criteria. A phase is complete only after its deliverables and relevant tests pass and you approve moving on.
 
 ## Confirmed scope decisions
 
 * **Local-first demo.** The working demonstration runs locally on Podman. The MVP is complete at Phase 6.
 * **Cloud is conceptual plus IaC.** The Azure architecture (APIM, VNet, private endpoints, managed identity) exists to show the intended security posture. It is expressed as Bicep that is authored and statically validated for Canada Central (`canadacentral`). The full stack is not deployed, because APIM, AI Search, and private networking carry significant monthly cost.
 * **Network slice is deployable.** A separately deployable subset of the IaC (VNet, subnets, NSGs, egress, private DNS, and low-cost private-endpoint services) is deployed to the user-provided Azure subscription to validate routing and DNS.
 * **Models.** Chat and embedding models are Microsoft Foundry deployments supplied by the user (endpoint and deployment names), reached through LiteLLM locally. No local models are used. Credentials are never committed.
 * **Search.** Local and cloud both use the user-provided Azure AI Search service. There is no local vector store (no PostgreSQL/pgvector), which removes the local-versus-cloud adapter mismatch. The local demo therefore depends on network access to Azure.
 * **IaC modules.** Use pinned Azure Verified Modules (AVM) where available, with thin composition modules otherwise.
 * **Subscription.** The user provides an Azure subscription for `validate`, `what-if`, and the network slice.
 
 ## Product outcome
 
 Deliver a demonstrable support assistant that answers questions about a documented, explicitly selected set of 100 OpenText products. Responses must be grounded in anonymously accessible source material, cite the source URL for each product or resource claim, and clearly disclose the limited demo catalog. The architecture should provide a safe path to later customer validation and production without representing the MVP as a production service.
 
 The longer-term OpenText Service Management expansion is an architectural consideration, not MVP scope.
 
 The demo runs locally. The Azure design is presented as a validated blueprint, with an explicit statement of which security controls are demonstrated locally and which are designed only.
 
 ## Approved repository structure
 
 Use a Python `src` layout for the backend and keep application code, tests, documentation, infrastructure, and automation distinct.
 
 ```text
 product-support-agent/
 ├── docs/
 │   ├── architecture/
 │   │   └── decisions/
 │   ├── security/
 │   ├── operations/
 │   └── implementation-plan.md
 ├── apps/
 │   └── web/
 │       ├── package.json
 │       ├── package-lock.json
 │       └── src/
 │           └── app/
 ├── src/
 │   └── product_support_agent/
 │       └── api/
 ├── tests/
 │   ├── unit/
 │   ├── integration/
 │   ├── end_to_end/
 │   ├── evaluation/
 │   └── fixtures/
 ├── infra/
 │   └── bicep/
 │       ├── modules/
 │       └── environments/
 ├── .github/
 │   ├── CODEOWNERS
 │   └── workflows/
 ├── pyproject.toml
 ├── uv.lock
 ├── compose.yaml
 ├── .env.example
 ├── README.md
 └── Instructions.md
 ```

 ### Phase 1: Repository foundation and local development
 
 **Status:** Implementation and automated verification are complete; phase-exit review is pending.
 
 Local Podman verification passed on 2026-11-21, including loopback bindings,
 MongoDB round trips and persistence, and authenticated Azurite operations with
 graceful stop/start persistence. The [local development guide](./operations/local-development.md)
 records the bare-restart limitation and verified shutdown procedure.
 GitHub-hosted CI remains unverified, and required merge enforcement is pending
 the [repository branch-protection backlog item](./operations/backlog.md).
 
 **Goal:** Establish a consistent, testable project foundation before implementing product behavior.
 
 **Scope and deliverables:**
 
 * Create the approved repository structure using Python `src` layout, a TypeScript Next.js app, and the selected package boundaries. Add CODEOWNERS and an ADR template. Branch protection remains a repository-host setting that must be enabled by an authorized maintainer.
 * Document supported Python version, dependency management, formatting, linting, type checking, configuration, and local run commands.
 * Define configuration and secret handling for local development; use Podman-compatible local service orchestration.
 * Establish test conventions, fixture policy, structured logging defaults, and correlation/run identifiers.
 * Add an initial GitHub Actions validation workflow for formatting, linting, typing, unit tests, dependency checks, and secret scanning. Pin every external action to a verified full commit SHA.
 * Add a local development guide and a concise architecture overview.
 
 **Verification and exit gate:**
 
 * A clean checkout can install dependencies and run the documented checks using the approved local toolchain.
 * A small test demonstrates that configuration, logging redaction hooks, and service health checks work without real source or model credentials.
 * The validation workflow blocks merge on required checks and does not expose secrets in logs.
 * You approve the structure, developer workflow, and baseline quality gates.
 
 **Depends on:** Phase 0 and Phase 0b approval.
 
 ### Phase 2: Source catalog and resilient ingestion
 
 **Status:** Implementation complete and the Phase 2 synthetic acceptance suite
 passes 56 tests. Live source verification and the manifest outcome are pending
 the approval gate. Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search credentials are local
 configuration inputs only and are not used by Phase 2 catalog or ingestion code.
 
 **Goal:** Reliably discover the catalog and enqueue exactly the approved 100 products without exceeding source limits.
 
 **Scope and deliverables:**
 
 * Implement catalog retrieval with explicit API/feed fallback rules, response validation, controlled pagination, deduplication, and empty-catalog handling.
 * Create versioned, reproducible selection of 100 products and make the manifest available to the chat experience.
 * Enqueue one product reference per message; keep queue payloads minimal and avoid embedding content in messages.
 * Implement a worker with source host allowlisting, safe URL validation, bounded downloads, status-aware handling, `Retry-After` support, bounded exponential backoff with jitter, and dead-letter reporting.
 * Skip authenticated/protected content without attempting to bypass access controls; record a minimal reason and outcome.
 * Store run-level and product-level ingestion status with enough provenance to diagnose success, skip, retry, and failure.
 * Treat 3xx redirects to login pages and 200 responses that contain login content as protected outcomes, not only 401 and 403. Azure Storage Queue has no built-in dead-letter queue, so implement a poison queue using the dequeue count, and add run-completion tracking and partial-failure semantics.
 * Start a versioned golden evaluation set tied to the manifest version; it grows in each later phase.
 
 **Verification and exit gate:**
 
 * Unit tests cover pagination, fallback decisions, empty results, duplicate products, URL validation, status handling, retry limits, and manifest reproducibility.
 * Integration tests use a local HTTP stub and queue emulator; they do not depend on OpenText availability.
 * A controlled end-to-end run proves no more than the approved manifest is processed and no protected content is stored.
 * You approve the resulting manifest and ingestion outcome report.
 
 **Depends on:** Phase 1 approval; Phase 0 source-access and manifest decisions.
 
 ### Phase 3: Canonical documents, indexing, and hybrid retrieval
 
 **Goal:** Turn permitted source material into traceable, updateable search results.
 
 **Scope and deliverables:**
 
 * Define and version canonical document and chunk schemas, stable IDs, content hashes, provenance, and update/delete behavior.
 * Implement parsing and normalization for approved public source formats; reject unsupported or oversized content safely.
 * Define chunking, metadata filters, embedding model/version, and index schema.
 * Implement the Azure AI Search provider behind a thin retrieval/indexing interface, plus an in-memory fake used by routine unit tests. Create and version the index definition as code and apply it with a script or the SDK.
 * Implement hybrid keyword, metadata, and semantic retrieval with configurable ranking and return source IDs, URLs, and excerpts.
 * Add index reconciliation and reprocessing for changed/deleted source content.
 
 **Verification and exit gate:**
 
 * Unit tests cover normalization, canonical identity, chunk provenance, schema evolution, and idempotent updates.
 * Integration tests verify indexing, metadata filters, hybrid retrieval, source URL preservation, and deletion/reindex behavior. They run against a dedicated Azure AI Search test index as controlled live tests; routine unit tests use the in-memory fake, and CI does not require Azure Search unless approved.
 * A reviewed retrieval test set meets agreed relevance and citation-source thresholds against Azure AI Search, using a dedicated test index separate from the demo index.
 * You approve schema, freshness behavior, and retrieval quality before agent integration.
 
 **Depends on:** Phase 2 approval; Phase 0 data ownership and retrieval decisions.
 
 ### Phase 4: FastAPI and grounded agent orchestration
 
 **Goal:** Answer product-support questions with bounded tools and verifiable citations.
 
 **Scope and deliverables:**
 
 * Implement FastAPI endpoints for health, catalog availability, and chat requests using validated request/response schemas.
 * Implement the Microsoft Agent Framework orchestration and structured retrieval tool/function calling behind the approved gateway interface. Verify the framework's release status and pin its version. Chat and embedding calls go through LiteLLM to the user-provided Microsoft Foundry deployments.
 * Enforce grounding: product/resource claims must map to retrieved source IDs and URLs; do not allow the model to create or alter citations.
 * Define behavior for no results, unsupported products, ambiguous requests, model/gateway failures, and inaccessible sources.
 * Treat retrieved documents as untrusted input; apply prompt-injection defenses, tool allowlisting, output validation, and safe error handling.
 * Add request limits, timeouts, concurrency controls, and provider-independent configuration.
 
 **Verification and exit gate:**
 
 * Unit tests cover tool input/output validation, citation binding, refusal/no-result behavior, prompt-injection cases, and model/gateway failure handling.
 * Integration tests use a deterministic fake model/gateway and search provider; no live model is required for routine tests.
 * End-to-end tests prove every factual product/resource response contains valid retrieved citations and unsupported claims are not presented as facts.
 * Abuse-case tests defined in Phase 0b pass for prompt injection, exfiltration through rendered output, citation spoofing, and quota abuse, and each threat-register entry owned by this phase has its verifying test.
 * You approve representative answers and the failure/refusal experience.
 
 **Depends on:** Phase 3 approval; Phase 0 gateway, identity, and safety decisions.
 
 ### Phase 5: Next.js interface and customer usefulness validation

 title: ADR-0002 Source Access and Product Manifest
 description: Proposed anonymous source access and stable demo-catalog policy
 author: Product Support Agent Team
 ms.date: 2026-11-21
 ms.topic: decision
 keywords:
   - ADR
   - ingestion
   - product manifest
 ---
 
 ## Status
 
 Phase 0 direction approved with a safe ingestion gate; the source probe remains
 inconclusive.
 
 ## Context
 
 The demo is limited to 100 products and must not bypass customer authorization or
 create undue load on OpenText. The initial bounded probe found an HTML listing
 response, a 401 search API response, and an unparsed JSON feed response.
 
 ## Proposed decision
 
 * Request only explicitly allowlisted public URLs with anonymous GETs.
 * Treat HTTP 401/403, login redirects, and login content as protected outcomes.
   Never retry them with credentials or follow a redirect to an authentication
   page.
 * Use the feed only when the listing and search API cannot yield a valid
   catalog. Do not confuse an authorization failure, parse failure, or empty
   result.
 * Generate a reproducible manifest of 100 products once per version and reuse
   it for normal reruns. Replacing the selection requires an explicit action.
 * Use `MAX_DEMO_PRODUCTS`, default 100 and hard maximum 100. Preserve the
   selected product IDs, names, and URLs, and display which products were
   successfully indexed.
 * Proposed default: sample from the full catalog without filtering for public
   resource availability. Show products with no permitted sources as uncovered,
   not as supported by invented content.
 * Keep request, page, concurrency, timeout, and response-size budgets bounded.
   Honor `Retry-After`; stop on unexpected source behavior.
 
 ## Alternatives considered
 
 * Resample randomly on every run: rejected because the demo and evaluation set
   would not be reproducible.
 * Filter out products without public resources: not selected as the proposed
   default because it can bias the sample and increase discovery traffic. This
   remains an open user decision.
 * Authenticate to access protected pages: rejected; outside MVP scope.
 
 ## Consequences
 
 The initial source behavior must be resolved before Phase 2. The user authorized
 up to 100 additional GET requests for bounded source verification/ingestion;
 that cap does not permit unrestricted crawling. A 100-product manifest does
 not imply that all products have indexed public resources. Accepted source
 terms, host allowlist, and per-run budgets must be recorded before ingestion.

 title: ADR-0004 Data Ownership and Privacy
 description: Proposed data ownership and telemetry minimization policy for the MVP
 author: Product Support Agent Team
 ms.date: 2026-11-21
 ms.topic: decision
 keywords:
   - ADR
   - privacy

 ---
 
 ## Status
 
 Phase 0 data-ownership direction approved. The retention policy remains subject
 to Phase 0b approval before collecting real user query content.
 
 ## Context
 
 The requested design includes MongoDB/Cosmos DB Mongo API, a queue, Azure AI
 Search, operational logs, and OpenTelemetry. The original requirements also ask
 to retain user queries and responses, but no purpose, notice, access, retention,
 or deletion policy is approved.
 
 ## Proposed decision
 
 * Use MongoDB as the proposed system of record for the local manifest, ingestion
   run status, product outcomes, and canonical documents.
 * Treat Azure AI Search as a derived index containing searchable chunks and
   provenance, not as the operational system of record.
 * Keep queue messages limited to product references and run identifiers.
 * Do not retain user queries or responses in logs, traces, or stored telemetry
   until privacy approval. The requested demo feature will have a global kill
   switch defaulting off and a per-session opt-out. Keep the UI's search history
   disabled.
 * Minimize operational telemetry to status, timing, component, correlation/run
   ID, and error category. Redact secrets and sensitive test values.
 
 ## Alternatives considered
 
 * Retain all query and response content by default: not selected because the
   required privacy controls and approval are not in place.
 * Use Azure AI Search as the source of truth for ingestion state: rejected
   because it is a retrieval index and does not own run lifecycle state.
 
 ## Consequences
 
 The user requests query/response retention for demo review, but retention is not
 enabled until the privacy impact assessment is approved. The assessment must
 specify the notice, access list, redaction behavior, retention period, and
 deletion process. Retention and deletion periods for canonical source content,
 run records, and operational telemetry remain open decisions.

 title: Product Support Agent Privacy Impact Assessment
 description: Draft privacy assessment for optional query and response retention in the local demo
 author: Product Support Agent Team
 ms.date: 2026-11-21
 ms.topic: reference
 keywords:
   - privacy
   - data retention
   - product support
 estimated_reading_time: 7
 ---
 
 ## Status and scope
 
 The user approved this Phase 0b assessment for a local, non-production demo,
 with the listed conditions. Query/response retention remains disabled until
 provider handling, reviewer access, notice, redaction, TTL, and deletion are
 verified. No real query or response content has been collected by this
 implementation work.
 
 ## Purpose and data flow
 
 The proposed purpose is limited to reviewing demo answer quality, investigating
 reported failures, and identifying abuse attempts. It is not approval for
 production analytics, marketing, user profiling, or unrelated model training.
 
 When enabled after approval, a restricted MongoDB collection may contain:
 
 * A redacted query and assistant response
 * A pseudonymous session/run identifier and timestamp
 * Retrieved evidence IDs and source URLs needed to verify citations
 * Model deployment identifier and non-sensitive operational status
 
 Do not store secrets, credentials, raw retrieved source text, browser identifiers,
 or personal identifiers beyond what is necessary for the approved purpose.
 OpenTelemetry logs and traces remain content-free.
 
 The query may also be sent to the user's LiteLLM and Foundry deployments to
 generate an answer. Their data handling, location, and retention settings must
 be verified separately. Local application retention controls do not control
 provider-side processing.
 
 ## Proposed controls
 
 | Control | Proposed behavior | Approval status |
 |---|---|---|
 | Global feature flag | `QUERY_RESPONSE_RETENTION_ENABLED` defaults to `false`; an operator may enable it only after policy and provider-handling approval. Setting it to `false` immediately stops new retention writes. | Proposed |
 | Session choice | When global retention is enabled, show a clear notice before each session. Retention is on for the session unless the user opts out. | User-selected; implementation pending |
 | Purpose limitation | Use retained content only for the demo-quality, troubleshooting, and safety-review purposes stated in the notice. | Proposed |
 | Redaction | Redact detected secrets and sensitive personal data before persistence. If redaction fails or its result is uncertain, do not retain the content; record only a non-sensitive failure reason. | User-selected; implementation pending |

 ## Draft user notice
 
 > This local demo may retain a redacted copy of your question and the assistant's
 > answer for demo quality and safety review for up to **[configured number of
 > days]** days. Do not enter personal information, customer information,
 > credentials, or confidential content. Retention is on for this session unless
 > you opt out. Your question is also sent to the configured Microsoft Foundry
 > deployment to generate an answer.
 
 The notice must be reviewed and finalized before retention is enabled. Confirm
 whether an explicit consent action is required for the intended demo audience.
 
 ## Data subject, access, and retention decisions
 
 * Data subjects are people using the local demo; the exact audience is not yet
   named.
 * No end-user authentication is planned for the local MVP. Restrict access at
   the operating-system and database boundary and do not expose the demo beyond
   local use.
 * The user selected a parameterized 7-day retention period and a
   parameterized reviewer role. A role-to-identity binding, legal/privacy
   approval, final notice wording, and deletion service level remain open.
 * Do not use retained content to train or fine-tune models.
 * Use synthetic or explicitly approved test content until all required policy
   approvals are recorded.
 
 ## Risk and residual limitations
 
 Redaction can miss sensitive content. A local demo can still be accessed by
 other users of the same machine or by a configured provider. The opt-out and
 global flag do not replace notice, access control, TTL enforcement, deletion
 tests, or provider data-handling review. Retention remains disabled until these
 controls are specified and approved.
 
 ## User approval checklist
 
 Before enabling retention, approve:
 
 1. Approve the 7-day default, parameter behavior, and deletion timing
 2. Bind `QUERY_REVIEWER_ROLE` to approved reviewer identities and database access
 3. Approve the notice and opt-out behavior
 4. Approve redaction scope and fail-closed behavior
 5. Verify Foundry/LiteLLM data-handling and residency settings
 6. Assign the incident owner and user-contact process
 
 The assessment must be approved before any real user query or response content
 is retained.

 ## Prerequisites
 
 * Python 3.11 or later
 * `uv` 0.13.9 or later
 * Node.js 20.9 or later and npm
 * Podman with a working `podman compose` provider for local MongoDB and Azurite
 
 The local application stack is not deployed to Azure. Catalog discovery and ingestion can run only against approved public sources
 and synthetic local HTTP/queue tests. Azure AI Search, model calls, and
 query/response retention are not enabled in the Phase 2 implementation.
 
 ## Configure the Python environment
 
 Copy `.env.example` to `.env` only if you need to change local settings. Do not
 commit `.env` or put user content in it, tests, or logs. Keep provider
 credentials in approved local environment configuration outside source control.
 
 ```powershell
 uv sync --all-groups
 uv run uvicorn product_support_agent.api.app:app --app-dir src --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
 ```
 
 The process health endpoint is available at
 `http://127.0.0.1:8000/healthz`. It reports API process health only; it does not
 validate databases, queues, search, or model-provider connectivity.
 The health response includes a generated `X-Request-ID`. Application log
 records use JSON fields for timestamp, level, logger, message, and request ID.
 
 The Phase 2 manifest endpoint is available at
 `http://127.0.0.1:8000/catalog/manifest`. Before catalog discovery is prepared,
 it returns a `null` manifest and the last catalog outcome. Ingestion run details
 are available at `/ingestion/runs/{run_id}`. Routine catalog and worker tests use
 HTTP mocks and in-memory fakes; they do not contact OpenText or Azure services.
 
 ## Run the frontend
 
 ```powershell
 Set-Location apps/web
 npm ci
 npm run dev
 ```
 
 Open `http://localhost:3000`. The Phase 1 page is a foundation placeholder and
 does not offer chat or product coverage claims.
 
 ## Start local data services
 
 From the repository root, start the emulated services when needed:
 
 ```powershell
 podman compose up -d mongodb azurite
 ```
 
 The services bind only to loopback. Stop and start them gracefully to preserve
 emulator metadata:
 
 ```powershell
 podman compose stop --timeout 30 mongodb azurite
 podman compose start mongodb azurite
 ```
 
 Azurite has a 30-second shutdown grace period in Compose. During verification,
 a bare `podman restart` lost newly written Azurite metadata; explicit graceful
 stop/start preserved it. Do not use a forced stop or bare restart for emulator
 data you need to keep. This emulator does not provide production durability.
 
 `podman compose down --timeout 30` stops and removes the project containers
 while preserving their named volumes. Adding `--volumes` removes their local
 data.
 
 ### Podman verification record
 
 Local verification passed on 2026-11-21 with Podman 5.6.2, a running WSL
 machine, and Docker Compose 2.34.0 as the external provider:
 
 * Compose validation, image pulls, and startup of MongoDB and Azurite passed.
 * Host listeners for ports 27017, 10000, and 10001 bound only to `127.0.0.1`.
 * MongoDB ping, synthetic document write/read, and restart persistence passed.
 * Authenticated Azurite queue and blob write/read through the host ports passed.
 * Azurite graceful stop/start preserved the message and blob. Message receipt,
   acknowledgement, and an empty-queue check passed.
 * Synthetic databases, queues, and blob containers were removed after testing.
 
 Only this project's containers were stopped after verification; named volumes
 and unrelated workloads were preserved. No OpenText or cloud services were
 accessed. GitHub-hosted CI and repository branch protection remain separate
 verification items in the [operations backlog](./backlog.md).

 ```powershell
 uv run ruff format --check .
 uv run ruff check .
 uv run mypy src/product_support_agent
 uv run pytest
 uv run bandit -q -r src
 uv run pip-audit --skip-editable
 ```
 
 ```powershell
 Set-Location apps/web
 npm run lint
 npm run typecheck
 npm run build
 npm audit --audit-level=high
 ```
 
 `npm run lint` runs Biome's formatting and lint checks on frontend source.
 
 Query and response retention defaults to off. Do not enable it until the
 privacy notice, reviewer identity, redaction behavior, deletion, TTL, and
 provider-handling approvals are complete. The Phase 1 app does not persist
 queries or responses.
 
 The logging filter redacts common labeled secrets (for example `api_key`,
 `client_secret`, `AccountKey`, and SAS `sig`), credentials in connection-string
 URIs, bearer tokens, JWTs, cookies, and email addresses. It also applies to the
 uvicorn server and access logs, which include request query strings. It is
 pattern-based and not a general-purpose PII detector, so never log query or
 response content.
 
 `npm run typecheck` runs `next typegen` first, so it works on a clean checkout
 before any `next build`. The repository's `.gitattributes` keeps LF line endings
 on Windows so that Biome and Ruff formatting checks match CI.

 ---
 title: ADR-0002 Source Access and Product Manifest
 description: Proposed anonymous source access and stable demo-catalog policy
 author: Product Support Agent Team
 ms.date: 2026-11-21
 ms.topic: decision
 keywords:
   - ADR
   - ingestion
   - product manifest
 ---
 
 ## Status
 
 Phase 0 direction approved with a safe ingestion gate; the source probe remains
 inconclusive.
 
 ## Context
 
 The demo is limited to 100 products and must not bypass customer authorization or
 create undue load on OpenText. The initial bounded probe found an HTML listing
 response, a 401 search API response, and an unparsed JSON feed response.
 
 ## Proposed decision
 
 * Request only explicitly allowlisted public URLs with anonymous GETs.
 * Treat HTTP 401/403, login redirects, and login content as protected outcomes.
   Never retry them with credentials or follow a redirect to an authentication
   page.
 * Use the feed only when the listing and search API cannot yield a valid
   catalog. Do not confuse an authorization failure, parse failure, or empty
   result.
 * Generate a reproducible manifest of 100 products once per version and reuse
   it for normal reruns. Replacing the selection requires an explicit action.
 * Use `MAX_DEMO_PRODUCTS`, default 100 and hard maximum 100. Preserve the
   selected product IDs, names, and URLs, and display which products were
   successfully indexed.
 * Proposed default: sample from the full catalog without filtering for public
   resource availability. Show products with no permitted sources as uncovered,
   not as supported by invented content.
 * Keep request, page, concurrency, timeout, and response-size budgets bounded.
   Honor `Retry-After`; stop on unexpected source behavior.
 
 ## Alternatives considered
 
 * Resample randomly on every run: rejected because the demo and evaluation set
   would not be reproducible.
 * Filter out products without public resources: not selected as the proposed
   default because it can bias the sample and increase discovery traffic. This
   remains an open user decision.
 * Authenticate to access protected pages: rejected; outside MVP scope.
 
 ## Consequences
 
 The initial source behavior must be resolved before Phase 2. The user authorized
 up to 100 additional GET requests for bounded source verification/ingestion;
 that cap does not permit unrestricted crawling. A 100-product manifest does
 not imply that all products have indexed public resources. Accepted source
 terms, host allowlist, and per-run budgets must be recorded before ingestion.

@'
import asyncio
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone

import httpx
from product_support_agent.catalog import FEED_URL, parse_feed, validate_source_url

MAX_BYTES = 4_194_304

async def main():
    if not validate_source_url(FEED_URL):
        raise SystemExit("Feed URL failed the source allowlist check")
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120.0, follow_redirects=False) as client:
        async with client.stream("GET", FEED_URL, headers={"Accept": "application/json"}) as response:
            print(f"status={response.status_code}")
            print(f"content_type={response.headers.get('content-type', '')}")
            print(f"content_length={response.headers.get('content-length', 'unknown')}")
            print(f"fetched_at={datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}")
            if response.status_code != 200:
                return
            if response.headers.get("location"):
                print("redirect_location_present=true")
                return
            chunks = []
            total = 0
            async for chunk in response.aiter_bytes():
                total += len(chunk)
                if total > MAX_BYTES:
                    print(f"response_bytes_exceeded_limit={MAX_BYTES}")
                    return
                chunks.append(chunk)
            body = b"".join(chunks)
    payload = json.loads(body)
    products = parse_feed(payload)
    print(f"response_bytes={len(body)}")
    print(f"top_level_type={type(payload).__name__}")
    print(f"parsed_product_count={len(products)}")
    if isinstance(payload, dict):
        print(f"top_level_keys={','.join(sorted(str(key) for key in payload.keys()))}")
    print(f"duplicate_free={len({p.product_id.lower() for p in products}) == len(products)}")
    print(f"sample_product_id={products[0].product_id if products else 'none'}")

asyncio.run(main())

 from datetime import UTC, datetime
 from uuid import uuid4
 
 from product_support_agent.catalog import CatalogClient, CatalogOutcome, Manifest, create_manifest
 from product_support_agent.queue import InMemoryQueue
 from product_support_agent.store import IngestionRun, InMemoryIngestionStore
 
 
 class PhaseTwoService:
     def __init__(
         self,
         *,
         catalog: CatalogClient,
         store: InMemoryIngestionStore,
         queue: InMemoryQueue,
         manifest_seed: str,
         max_demo_products: int,
     ) -> None:
         self.catalog = catalog
         self.store = store
         self.queue = queue
         self.manifest_seed = manifest_seed
         self.max_demo_products = max_demo_products
         self.manifest: Manifest | None = None
         self.catalog_outcome: CatalogOutcome | None = None
 
     async def discover_and_prepare(self) -> tuple[Manifest | None, CatalogOutcome]:
         outcome = await self.catalog.discover()
         self.catalog_outcome = outcome
         if not outcome.products:
             return None, outcome
 
         manifest = create_manifest(
             outcome.products,
             manifest_version=f"demo-{datetime.now(UTC).strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}",
             seed=self.manifest_seed,
             selection_timestamp=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
             max_products=self.max_demo_products,
         )
         self.manifest = manifest
         return manifest, outcome
 
     def enqueue_manifest(self, run_id: str | None = None) -> IngestionRun:
         if self.manifest is None:
             raise RuntimeError("a manifest must be prepared before enqueueing")
         active_run_id = run_id or str(uuid4())
         now = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
         run = IngestionRun(
             run_id=active_run_id,
             manifest_version=self.manifest.manifest_version,
             started_at=now,
         )
         self.store.start_run(run)
         for product in self.manifest.selected_products:
             self.queue.send_product_reference(active_run_id, product.product_id)
         return run

 # Markdown Instructions
 
 These instructions define the Markdown style guide enforced by markdownlint in this codebase. Follow them when creating or updating any `.md` file here. Examples are included in XML-style blocks that downstream tools can extract.
 
 ## Scope
 
 * Applies to all Markdown files in this codebase excluding files with `<!-- markdownlint-disable-file -->`.
 * Mirrors the active configuration in `.markdownlint.json`.
 * When in doubt, prefer clarity and consistency. Automated fixes are acceptable if they preserve intent.
 
 ## General conventions
 
 * Use UTF-8 and plain ASCII punctuation unless content requires otherwise.
 * Prefer descriptive headings and concise paragraphs; avoid trailing or leading extra spaces.
 * Keep lines reasonably short for readability; wrap where sensible without breaking URLs or code.
 
 ## Headings
 
 * Start documents with a single level-1 heading that acts as the title when appropriate.
 * Increase heading levels by one at a time; do not skip levels.
 * Use a consistent heading style per file. Prefer ATX style (`#`, `##`, `###`, ...) for new content.
 * Do not indent headings; they must start at column 1.
 * Surround each heading with a blank line above and below (except at file start/end).
 * Do not end headings with punctuation such as `. , ; : !` or their full-width variants.
 * Avoid duplicate headings under the same parent section; make them unique.
 * Do NOT use an H1 heading when YAML frontmatter contains a `title:` field. The frontmatter title satisfies MD025 and MD041. Start content with H2 or below after frontmatter. If no frontmatter exists, begin the file with a top-level heading.
 * Use exactly one space after the `#` characters in headings; do not omit or use multiple spaces.
 * If you close ATX headings with trailing `#` characters, use a single space between the text and both the opening and closing hashes; do not use multiple spaces on either side.
 * Use only one top-level heading per document; subsequent sections must use lower levels.
 
 <!-- <example-headings> -->
 ```markdown
 # Title
 
 ## Section
 
 ### Subsection
 ```
 <!-- </example-headings> -->
 
 ## YAML Frontmatter
 
 * All markdown files MUST include YAML frontmatter at the beginning of the file
 * Frontmatter MUST be the first content in the file (before H1 heading)
 * Use triple-dash delimiters (---) on separate lines to wrap frontmatter YAML
 * Frontmatter provides machine-readable metadata for validation, SEO, and site generation
 * Do NOT use an H1 heading when frontmatter includes a `title:` field; the title in frontmatter acts as the document title per MD025/MD041
 * Start document content with H2 or below when frontmatter contains a `title:` field
 
 ### Required Fields by File Type
 
 | File Type                                               | Required Fields          | Schema File                              |
 |---------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|------------------------------------------|
 | Root community files (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, etc.) | `title`, `description`   | `root-community-frontmatter.schema.json` |
 | Documentation files (`docs/**/*.md`)                    | `title`, `description`   | `docs-frontmatter.schema.json`           |
 | Instruction files (`.github/**/*.instructions.md`)      | `description`, `applyTo` | `instruction-frontmatter.schema.json`    |
 | Agent files (`.github/**/*.agent.md`)                   | `description`            | `agent-frontmatter.schema.json`          |
 | Prompt files (`.github/**/*.prompt.md`)                 | `description`            | `prompt-frontmatter.schema.json`         |
 
 ### Recommended Fields
 
 * `author`: Author or team responsible for the content
 * `ms.date`: Last modified date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD)
 * `ms.topic`: Documentation topic type (overview, concept, tutorial, reference, how-to, troubleshooting)
 * `keywords`: Array of keywords for content categorization
 * `estimated_reading_time`: Positive integer (minutes)
 
 ### Date Format
 
 * MUST use ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., `ms.date: 2025-11-15`)
 * Do NOT use MM/DD/YYYY, DD/MM/YYYY, or other formats
 
 ### Schema Validation
 
 * Schemas are located in `scripts/linting/schemas/`
 * Pattern-based mapping in `schema-mapping.json` determines which schema applies to each file
 * VS Code YAML extension (`redhat.vscode-yaml`) provides in-editor validation
 * Run validation: `npm run validate:frontmatter` or `pwsh scripts/linting/Validate-MarkdownFrontmatter.ps1`
 
 ### Schema Pattern Matching
 
 Files are validated against schemas based on glob pattern matching:
 
 * Patterns are evaluated in order from most specific to least specific
 * First matching pattern determines the schema
 * If no pattern matches, `base-frontmatter.schema.json` is used as default
 * Pattern syntax supports:
   * `**` for recursive directory matching
   * `*` for single path segment wildcard
   * `|` for alternation (e.g., `README.md|CONTRIBUTING.md`)
 
 Pattern examples:
 
 * `.github/**/*.instructions.md` - All instruction files in .github directory tree
 * `docs/**/*.md` - All markdown files under docs directory
 * `README.md|CONTRIBUTING.md` - Exact filename match (alternation)
 
 ### Examples
 
 <!-- <example-frontmatter-docs> -->
 ```yaml
 ---
 title: Getting Started with HVE Core
 description: Quick setup guide for using HVE Core Copilot customizations in your projects
 author: Microsoft
 ms.date: 2025-11-15
 ms.topic: tutorial
 keywords:
   - github copilot
   - setup
   - getting started
 estimated_reading_time: 5
 ---
 
 # Getting Started with HVE Core
 
 This guide shows you how to configure your project...
 ```
 <!-- </example-frontmatter-docs> -->
 
 <!-- <example-frontmatter-instructions> -->

 ```yaml
 ---
 
 # Markdown Instructions
 
 These instructions define the Markdown style guide...
 ```
 <!-- </example-frontmatter-instructions> -->
 
 ## Lists
 
 * Use unordered list markers consistently across a file; for the same level, do not mix `*`, `+`, `-`.
   * Try to always use `*` for unordered lists.
   * Avoid using `-` and `+` for unordered lists unless the file already uses these.
 * Indent unordered sublist content by 2 spaces per level.
 * Keep indentation consistent for items at the same nesting level.
 * Use one space between any list marker and the list text for both ordered and unordered lists.
 * Surround lists with a blank line before and after (unless at file start/end).
 * For ordered lists, either use `1.` for all items or increment numerically; do not mix styles within a list. Leading zeros are allowed only when used consistently.
 
 <!-- <example-lists> -->
 ```markdown
 * Item 1
 * Item 2
   * Nested item
 
 1. Step
 2. Step
 3. Step
 ```
 <!-- </example-lists> -->
 
 ### Bullet point punctuation
 
 Follow professional editorial standards for bullet point punctuation consistency:
 
 * **Fragment bullet points** (short phrases, technical terms, simple commands): Do NOT end with periods.
 * **Complete sentence bullet points** (subject + verb constructions): End with periods.
 * Based on Google, Microsoft, and GitLab style guidelines
 
 <!-- <example-bullet-punctuation> -->
 ```markdown
 * Configuration file
 * API endpoint
 * User authentication
 * Enable debugging mode
 
 * This function validates the input parameters
 * The system processes requests asynchronously
 * Users can configure settings through the UI
 * When enabled, it provides detailed logging information
 ```
 <!-- </example-bullet-punctuation> -->
 
 ## Code blocks and code spans
 
 * Use fenced code blocks consistently (prefer triple backticks) and surround them with a blank line before and after. Use fenced code instead of indented code blocks.
 * Always specify a language for fenced code blocks; use `text` if no highlighting is desired.
 * Avoid tabs; use spaces everywhere. Do not include hard tab characters in code, lists, or text.
 * Do not add spaces just inside backticks of code spans; write `` `code` `` not `` ` code ` ``.
 * For shell examples, do not prefix commands with `$` unless you also show the command output; prefer copy-pasteable commands without the prompt.
 * Use backticks for code fences consistently across the repository; do not use tildes.
 
 <!-- <example-code> -->
 ````markdown
 ```bash
 # Good
 echo "Hello"
 ```
 
 Some inline `code` here.
 ````
 <!-- </example-code> -->
 
 ## Links and images
 
 * Do not reverse link syntax; write `[text](url)`.
 * Do not use empty links like `[]()` or `(#)`; always provide a valid destination.
 * Avoid bare URLs; wrap them in angle brackets like `<https://example.com>` or make them proper links with text.
 * Ensure link fragments match generated heading IDs (kebab-case, lower-case). Use `<a id="...">` when needed.
 * Provide alternate text for all images. If an image must be hidden from assistive tech, use `aria-hidden="true"` in HTML.
 * Keep spaces out of link text brackets: `[text]`, not `[ text ]`.
 * Use a consistent link/image style within a document. Inline and autolink styles are allowed. When using full `[text][label]` or collapsed `[label][]` references, ensure the corresponding `[label]: URL` is defined. Remove unused or duplicate reference definitions.
 * If literal bracketed text is intended (not a link), escape the brackets as `\[text\]`.
 
 <!-- <example-links-images> -->
 ```markdown
 See <https://example.com> and [Docs](https://example.com/docs).
 
 ![Diagram](./diagram.png)
 ```
 <!-- </example-links-images> -->
 
 ## Spacing and blank lines
 
 * Limit paragraph and prose lines to approximately 500 characters; keep headings under 80 characters.
 * Do not add trailing spaces at the end of lines except when intentionally forcing a hard line break; when forcing breaks, use exactly two spaces.
 * Do not use multiple consecutive blank lines; keep at most one in a row.
 * Surround fenced code blocks, headings, lists, and tables with a blank line before and after (unless at file start/end).
 * Files must end with a single newline; no extra blank lines at EOF.
 * Do not break long URLs or long words to satisfy line length. Headings should honor their shorter limit; tables are exempt from line length checks. Code blocks may exceed normal line length; avoid wrapping code for width alone.
 
 ## Blockquotes
 
 * Use a single space after the `>` marker; avoid multiple spaces.
 * Do not place a bare blank line between adjacent blockquotes unless they are the same quote (then include `>` on the blank line to continue it).
 * Inside blockquotes, apply the same list and code rules; when creating tight lists with code fences inside blockquotes, consider whether a blank line is required for your target renderer.
 
 <!-- <example-blockquotes> -->
 ```markdown
 > Quoted text continues
 >
 > Same quote after a blank line.
 ```
 <!-- </example-blockquotes> -->
 
 ## Horizontal rules
 
 * Use one horizontal rule style consistently within a document. Prefer `---`.
 
 ## Emphasis
 
 * Use a consistent style for emphasis and strong emphasis throughout a document. Prefer `*italic*` and `**bold**` for new content.
 * Do not put spaces inside emphasis markers: `**bold**`, not `** bold **`.
 * Do not use emphasis-only lines as section separators; use proper headings instead.
  * Avoid emphasis within words using underscores; prefer asterisks for word-internal emphasis if absolutely necessary.
 
 ## Tables
 
 * Surround tables with a blank line before and after (unless at file start/end).
 * Use a consistent pipe style; prefer leading and trailing pipes on all rows.
 * Ensure every row has the same number of cells as the header.
 * Keep header and delimiter rows aligned in column count so the table is recognized by renderers.
 * Use aligned column style: all pipe characters must align vertically across all rows. Pad cell content with spaces so pipes line up.
 
 <!-- <example-tables> -->
 ```markdown
 | Column A | Column B | Column C |
 |----------|----------|----------|
 | Short    | Medium   | Longer   |
 | A        | BB       | CCC      |
 ```
 <!-- </example-tables> -->
 
 ## Miscellaneous
 
 * Do not include inline HTML unless necessary; if used, limit to explicitly allowed elements like `<details>` and `<summary>` in this repository.
 * Fenced code blocks must declare a language; use a recognized language name. If no highlighting is desired, use `text`.
 * Follow proper capitalization for product and technology names used in this repository (e.g., "GitHub", "JavaScript").
  * Avoid using inline HTML when a Markdown equivalent exists. If an inline HTML element is necessary and allowed, keep it minimal and well-formed.
 * Ensure files end with exactly one trailing newline character.
 * Use a consistent fence marker for code blocks (backticks) across a file.
 * Use a consistent emphasis style throughout a file (prefer asterisks for both italic and bold).
 * Validate intra-document link fragments; they must match the generated IDs of headings or explicitly provided anchors. Prefer lower-case, dash-separated fragments.
 * When using reference-style links or images, ensure the referenced labels are defined. Remove any unused or duplicate reference definitions. Keep the special checkbox syntax `[x]` intact.
 * Link and image styles allowed: autolinks `<https://...>`, inline `[text](url)`, and reference `[text][label]`/`[label][]`. Avoid bare URLs in text; prefer autolink syntax. Avoid inline links where the link text equals the same absolute URL with no title; prefer autolink.
 * For tables, apply a consistent leading/trailing pipe style; prefer both leading and trailing pipes. Ensure all rows have the same number of cells as the header.

 from __future__ import annotations
 
 from datetime import UTC, datetime
 from uuid import uuid4
 
 from product_support_agent.catalog import CatalogClient, CatalogOutcome, Manifest, create_manifest
 from product_support_agent.queue import InMemoryQueue
 from product_support_agent.store import IngestionRun, InMemoryIngestionStore
 
 
 class PhaseTwoService:
     def __init__(
         self,
         *,
         catalog: CatalogClient,
         store: InMemoryIngestionStore,
         queue: InMemoryQueue,
         manifest_seed: str,
         max_demo_products: int,
     ) -> None:
         self.catalog = catalog
         self.store = store
         self.queue = queue
         self.manifest_seed = manifest_seed
         self.max_demo_products = max_demo_products
         self.manifest: Manifest | None = None
         self.catalog_outcome: CatalogOutcome | None = None
 
     async def discover_and_prepare(self) -> tuple[Manifest | None, CatalogOutcome]:
         outcome = await self.catalog.discover()
         self.catalog_outcome = outcome
         if not outcome.products:
             return None, outcome
 
         manifest = create_manifest(
             outcome.products,
             manifest_version=f"demo-{datetime.now(UTC).strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}",
             seed=self.manifest_seed,
             selection_timestamp=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
             max_products=self.max_demo_products,
         )
         self.manifest = manifest
         return manifest, outcome
 
     def enqueue_manifest(self, run_id: str | None = None) -> IngestionRun:
         if self.manifest is None:
             raise RuntimeError("a manifest must be prepared before enqueueing")
         active_run_id = run_id or str(uuid4())
         now = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
         run = IngestionRun(
             run_id=active_run_id,
             manifest_version=self.manifest.manifest_version,
             started_at=now,
         )
         self.store.start_run(run)
         for product in self.manifest.selected_products:
             self.queue.send_product_reference(active_run_id, product.product_id)
         return run

@'
import asyncio
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
from product_support_agent.catalog import FEED_URL, create_manifest, parse_feed, validate_source_url

MAX_BYTES = 4_194_304
SEED = "approved-demo-v1"
VERSION = "opentext-2026-11-21-v1"
OUTPUT = Path("docs/operations/phase-2-product-manifest-v1.json")

async def main():
    if not validate_source_url(FEED_URL):
        raise SystemExit("Feed URL failed the source allowlist check")
    chunks = []
    total = 0
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120.0, follow_redirects=False) as client:
        async with client.stream("GET", FEED_URL, headers={"Accept": "application/json"}) as response:
            if response.status_code != 200:
                raise SystemExit(f"Feed request failed with HTTP {response.status_code}")
            if response.headers.get("location"):
                raise SystemExit("Feed unexpectedly returned a redirect")
            async for chunk in response.aiter_bytes():
                total += len(chunk)
                if total > MAX_BYTES:
                    raise SystemExit(f"Feed exceeded the {MAX_BYTES}-byte decompressed response limit")
                chunks.append(chunk)
            fetched_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    body = b"".join(chunks)
    payload = json.loads(body)
    products = parse_feed(payload)
    if not products:
        raise SystemExit("The feed returned no parseable products")
    manifest = create_manifest(
        products,
        manifest_version=VERSION,
        seed=SEED,
        selection_timestamp=fetched_at,
        max_products=100,
    )
    OUTPUT.write_text(
        json.dumps(manifest.model_dump(mode="json"), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print(f"manifest={OUTPUT}")
    print(f"version={manifest.manifest_version}")
    print(f"feed_products={len(products)} selected_products={len(manifest.selected_products)}")
    print(f"feed_sha256={hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()}")
    print(f"selection_timestamp={manifest.selection_timestamp}")
    print(f"first_selected={manifest.selected_products[0].product_id}:{manifest.selected_products[0].slug}")
    print(f"distinct_id_slug={sum(p.product_id != p.slug for p in products)}")

asyncio.run(main())
'@ | & .venv\Scripts\python.exe -

@'
import asyncio
import json
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from product_support_agent.catalog import Manifest, validate_source_url
from product_support_agent.queue import InMemoryQueue
from product_support_agent.store import InMemoryIngestionStore
from product_support_agent.worker import IngestionWorker

MANIFEST_PATH = Path("docs/operations/phase-2-product-manifest-v1.json")
REPORT_JSON = Path("docs/operations/phase-2-ingestion-outcome-v1.json")
REPORT_MD = Path("docs/operations/phase-2-ingestion-outcome-v1.md")
REQUEST_CAP = 100
FEED_GETS_ALREADY_USED = 3
MAX_PAGE_GETS = REQUEST_CAP - FEED_GETS_ALREADY_USED
DELAY_SECONDS = 1.0

async def main():
    manifest = Manifest.model_validate_json(MANIFEST_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if len(manifest.selected_products) != 100:
        raise SystemExit("The live manifest must contain exactly 100 products")
    if not all(validate_source_url(str(product.source_url)) for product in manifest.selected_products):
        raise SystemExit("Manifest contains a URL outside the approved source allowlist")

    started_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    run_id = "opentext-live-2026-11-21-v1"
    worker = IngestionWorker(
        queue=InMemoryQueue(),
        store=InMemoryIngestionStore(),
        max_attempts=1,
        timeout_seconds=8.0,
        max_download_bytes=4_194_304,
    )
    results = []
    stop_reason = "request_budget_exhausted"

    for index, product in enumerate(manifest.selected_products):
        if index >= MAX_PAGE_GETS:
            break
        result = await worker._fetch(str(product.source_url))
        results.append({
            "product_id": product.product_id,
            "name": product.name,
            "slug": product.slug,
            "source_url": str(product.source_url),
            **result,
        })
        reason = result["reason_category"]
        status = result["http_status"]
        if status == 429:
            stop_reason = "upstream_rate_limited; stopped without retry"
            break
        if status is not None and 500 <= status < 600:
            stop_reason = "upstream_server_error; stopped without retry"
            break
        if reason == "network_error":
            stop_reason = "network_error; stopped without retry"
            break
        if index + 1 < MAX_PAGE_GETS:
            await asyncio.sleep(DELAY_SECONDS)

    attempted_ids = {row["product_id"] for row in results}
    for product in manifest.selected_products:
        if product.product_id not in attempted_ids:
            results.append({
                "product_id": product.product_id,
                "name": product.name,
                "slug": product.slug,
                "source_url": str(product.source_url),
                "outcome": "not_attempted",
                "reason_category": stop_reason,
                "http_status": None,
                "attempt_count": 0,
            })

    completed_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    counts = Counter(row["outcome"] for row in results)
    report = {
        "report_schema_version": 1,
        "phase": 2,
        "run_id": run_id,
        "manifest_version": manifest.manifest_version,
        "started_at": started_at,
        "completed_at": completed_at,
        "source": {
            "catalog_url": "https://my.opentext.com/api/web/feed/product",
            "catalog_http_status": 200,
            "catalog_content_type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
            "catalog_decoded_response_bytes": 3346806,
            "catalog_parseable_unique_products": 1302,
            "catalog_decoded_payload_sha256": "8f0ce0794784c2315089e8692d17cf49c1ed5bc15a854e5e81da6d51c75ce526",
            "catalog_fetched_at": manifest.selection_timestamp,
        },
        "request_budget": {
            "approved_additional_get_limit": REQUEST_CAP,
            "feed_gets_used_before_product_checks": FEED_GETS_ALREADY_USED,
            "product_page_get_limit": MAX_PAGE_GETS,
            "product_page_gets_attempted": sum(row["attempt_count"] for row in results),
            "total_gets_used": FEED_GETS_ALREADY_USED + sum(row["attempt_count"] for row in results),
            "sequential_delay_seconds": DELAY_SECONDS,
            "retry_policy": "One attempt per product; stop the run on 429, 5xx, or network error to stay within the approved request budget.",
        },
        "summary": {
            "manifest_products": len(manifest.selected_products),
            "attempted_products": len(attempted_ids),
            "not_attempted_products": len(manifest.selected_products) - len(attempted_ids),
            "outcome_counts": dict(sorted(counts.items())),
            "stop_reason": stop_reason,
            "response_bodies_persisted": False,
            "protected_content_persisted": False,
            "search_index_updated": False,
        },
        "products": results,
    }
    REPORT_JSON.write_text(
        json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )

    outcome_rows = "\n".join(
        f"| {key} | {value} |" for key, value in sorted(counts.items())
    ) or "| none | 0 |"
    md = f'''---
title: Phase 2 Live Ingestion Outcome Report
description: Live OpenText feed and product-page outcome summary for the Phase 2 manifest
author: Product Support Agent Team
ms.date: 2026-11-21
ms.topic: reference
keywords:
  - ingestion
  - OpenText
  - manifest
---

## Summary

This report records live anonymous GET results for the OpenText product feed and the selected product URLs. It contains status metadata only; response bodies were not persisted. The product-page checks used the actual manifest and no mock or stub source data.

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Manifest | [Phase 2 product manifest](./phase-2-product-manifest-v1.json), version `{manifest.manifest_version}` |
| Product catalog | 1,302 unique parseable products from HTTP 200 |
| Manifest size | 100 products |
| Product pages attempted | {len(attempted_ids)} of 100 |
| Feed GETs already used | {FEED_GETS_ALREADY_USED} |
| Product-page GETs used | {sum(row["attempt_count"] for row in results)} |
| Total against approved 100-GET budget | {FEED_GETS_ALREADY_USED + sum(row["attempt_count"] for row in results)} |
| Stop reason | {stop_reason} |
| Search indexing | Not performed; indexing belongs to Phase 3 |

### Product-page outcomes

| Outcome | Count |
|---|---:|
{outcome_rows}

### Safety and limitations

* Requests were sequential, used the `my.opentext.com` HTTPS allowlist, did not follow redirects, and were limited to one attempt per product. The run stops on rate limiting, a server error, or a network error.
* The response-size limit was 4 MiB. Response bodies were inspected only in memory to classify protected login content; no page content or embeddings were stored.
* The live run did not update Azure AI Search. A successful download is not evidence that content was parsed, normalized, indexed, or retrievable.
* Products with `not_attempted` outcomes remain unverified. Their records and all HTTP status details are in the [machine-readable outcome report](./phase-2-ingestion-outcome-v1.json).

The feed payload SHA-256 is `{report["source"]["catalog_decoded_payload_sha256"]}`. The decoded response was {report["source"]["catalog_decoded_response_bytes"]} bytes, within the configured 4 MiB limit.
'''
    REPORT_MD.write_text(md, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    print(f"manifest_products={len(manifest.selected_products)}")
    print(f"product_page_attempts={sum(row['attempt_count'] for row in results)}")
    print(f"total_gets_used={report['request_budget']['total_gets_used']}")
    print(f"outcome_counts={dict(sorted(counts.items()))}")
    print(f"stop_reason={stop_reason}")
    print(f"report_json={REPORT_JSON}")
    print(f"report_markdown={REPORT_MD}")

asyncio.run(main())
'@ | & .venv\Scripts\python.exe -

 ### Phase 2: Source catalog and resilient ingestion
 
 **Status:** Implementation complete and the Phase 2 synthetic acceptance suite
 passes 56 tests. Live source verification and the manifest outcome are pending
 the approval gate. Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search credentials are local
 configuration inputs only and are not used by Phase 2 catalog or ingestion code.
 
 **Goal:** Reliably discover the catalog and enqueue exactly the approved 100 products without exceeding source limits.
 
 **Scope and deliverables:**
 
 * Implement catalog retrieval with explicit API/feed fallback rules, response validation, controlled pagination, deduplication, and empty-catalog handling.
 * Create versioned, reproducible selection of 100 products and make the manifest available to the chat experience.
 * Enqueue one product reference per message; keep queue payloads minimal and avoid embedding content in messages.
 * Implement a worker with source host allowlisting, safe URL validation, bounded downloads, status-aware handling, `Retry-After` support, bounded exponential backoff with jitter, and dead-letter reporting.
 * Skip authenticated/protected content without attempting to bypass access controls; record a minimal reason and outcome.
 * Store run-level and product-level ingestion status with enough provenance to diagnose success, skip, retry, and failure.
 * Treat 3xx redirects to login pages and 200 responses that contain login content as protected outcomes, not only 401 and 403. Azure Storage Queue has no built-in dead-letter queue, so implement a poison queue using the dequeue count, and add run-completion tracking and partial-failure semantics.
 * Start a versioned golden evaluation set tied to the manifest version; it grows in each later phase.
 
 **Verification and exit gate:**
 
 * Unit tests cover pagination, fallback decisions, empty results, duplicate products, URL validation, status handling, retry limits, and manifest reproducibility.
 * Integration tests use a local HTTP stub and queue emulator; they do not depend on OpenText availability.
 * A controlled end-to-end run proves no more than the approved manifest is processed and no protected content is stored.
 * You approve the resulting manifest and ingestion outcome report.
 
 **Depends on:** Phase 1 approval; Phase 0 source-access and manifest decisions.

 title: ADR-0002 Source Access and Product Manifest
 description: Proposed anonymous source access and stable demo-catalog policy
 author: Product Support Agent Team
 ms.date: 2026-11-21
 ms.topic: decision
 keywords:
   - ADR
   - ingestion
   - product manifest
 ---
 
 ## Status
 
 Phase 0 direction approved with a safe ingestion gate; the source probe remains
 inconclusive.
 
 ## Context
 
 The demo is limited to 100 products and must not bypass customer authorization or
 create undue load on OpenText. The initial bounded probe found an HTML listing
 response, a 401 search API response, and an unparsed JSON feed response.
 
 ## Proposed decision
 
 * Request only explicitly allowlisted public URLs with anonymous GETs.
 * Treat HTTP 401/403, login redirects, and login content as protected outcomes.
   Never retry them with credentials or follow a redirect to an authentication
   page.
 * Use the feed only when the listing and search API cannot yield a valid
   catalog. Do not confuse an authorization failure, parse failure, or empty
   result.
 * Generate a reproducible manifest of 100 products once per version and reuse
   it for normal reruns. Replacing the selection requires an explicit action.
 * Use `MAX_DEMO_PRODUCTS`, default 100 and hard maximum 100. Preserve the
   selected product IDs, names, and URLs, and display which products were
   successfully indexed.
 * Proposed default: sample from the full catalog without filtering for public
   resource availability. Show products with no permitted sources as uncovered,
   not as supported by invented content.
 * Keep request, page, concurrency, timeout, and response-size budgets bounded.
   Honor `Retry-After`; stop on unexpected source behavior.
 
 ## Alternatives considered
 
 * Resample randomly on every run: rejected because the demo and evaluation set
   would not be reproducible.
 * Filter out products without public resources: not selected as the proposed
   default because it can bias the sample and increase discovery traffic. This
   remains an open user decision.
 * Authenticate to access protected pages: rejected; outside MVP scope.
 
 ## Consequences
 
 The initial source behavior must be resolved before Phase 2. The user authorized
 up to 100 additional GET requests for bounded source verification/ingestion;
 that cap does not permit unrestricted crawling. A 100-product manifest does
 not imply that all products have indexed public resources. Accepted source
 terms, host allowlist, and per-run budgets must be recorded before ingestion.

 * Implement catalog retrieval with explicit API/feed fallback rules, response validation, controlled pagination, deduplication, and empty-catalog handling.
 * Create versioned, reproducible selection of 100 products and make the manifest available to the chat experience.
 * Enqueue one product reference per message; keep queue payloads minimal and avoid embedding content in messages.
 * Implement a worker with source host allowlisting, safe URL validation, bounded downloads, status-aware handling, `Retry-After` support, bounded exponential backoff with jitter, and dead-letter reporting.
 * Skip authenticated/protected content without attempting to bypass access controls; record a minimal reason and outcome.
 * Store run-level and product-level ingestion status with enough provenance to diagnose success, skip, retry, and failure.
 * Treat 3xx redirects to login pages and 200 responses that contain login content as protected outcomes, not only 401 and 403. Azure Storage Queue has no built-in dead-letter queue, so implement a poison queue using the dequeue count, and add run-completion tracking and partial-failure semantics.
 * Start a versioned golden evaluation set tied to the manifest version; it grows in each later phase.
 
 **Verification and exit gate:**
 
 * Unit tests cover pagination, fallback decisions, empty results, duplicate products, URL validation, status handling, retry limits, and manifest reproducibility.
 * Integration tests use a local HTTP stub and queue emulator; they do not depend on OpenText availability.

 title: ADR-0002 Source Access and Product Manifest
 description: Proposed anonymous source access and stable demo-catalog policy
 author: Product Support Agent Team
 ms.date: 2026-11-21
 ms.topic: decision
 keywords:
   - ADR
   - ingestion
   - product manifest
 ---
 
 ## Status
 
 Phase 0 direction approved with a safe ingestion gate; the source probe remains
 inconclusive.
 
 ## Context
 
 The demo is limited to 100 products and must not bypass customer authorization or
 create undue load on OpenText. The initial bounded probe found an HTML listing
 response, a 401 search API response, and an unparsed JSON feed response.
 
 ## Proposed decision
 
 * Request only explicitly allowlisted public URLs with anonymous GETs.
 * Treat HTTP 401/403, login redirects, and login content as protected outcomes.
   Never retry them with credentials or follow a redirect to an authentication
   page.
 * Use the feed only when the listing and search API cannot yield a valid
   catalog. Do not confuse an authorization failure, parse failure, or empty
   result.
 * Generate a reproducible manifest of 100 products once per version and reuse
   it for normal reruns. Replacing the selection requires an explicit action.
 * Use `MAX_DEMO_PRODUCTS`, default 100 and hard maximum 100. Preserve the
   selected product IDs, names, and URLs, and display which products were
   successfully indexed.
 * Proposed default: sample from the full catalog without filtering for public
   resource availability. Show products with no permitted sources as uncovered,
   not as supported by invented content.
 * Keep request, page, concurrency, timeout, and response-size budgets bounded.
   Honor `Retry-After`; stop on unexpected source behavior.
 
 ## Alternatives considered
 
 * Resample randomly on every run: rejected because the demo and evaluation set
   would not be reproducible.
 * Filter out products without public resources: not selected as the proposed
   default because it can bias the sample and increase discovery traffic. This
   remains an open user decision.
 * Authenticate to access protected pages: rejected; outside MVP scope.
 
 ## Consequences
 
 The initial source behavior must be resolved before Phase 2. The user authorized
 up to 100 additional GET requests for bounded source verification/ingestion;
 that cap does not permit unrestricted crawling. A 100-product manifest does
 not imply that all products have indexed public resources. Accepted source
 terms, host allowlist, and per-run budgets must be recorded before ingestion.

 ## Status
 
 Phase 0 direction approved with a safe ingestion gate; the source probe remains
 inconclusive.
 
 ## Context
 
 The demo is limited to 100 products and must not bypass customer authorization or
 create undue load on OpenText. The initial bounded probe found an HTML listing
 response, a 401 search API response, and an unparsed JSON feed response.
 
 ## Proposed decision
 
 * Request only explicitly allowlisted public URLs with anonymous GETs.
 * Treat HTTP 401/403, login redirects, and login content as protected outcomes.
   Never retry them with credentials or follow a redirect to an authentication
   page.
 * Use the feed only when the listing and search API cannot yield a valid
   catalog. Do not confuse an authorization failure, parse failure, or empty
   result.
 * Generate a reproducible manifest of 100 products once per version and reuse
   it for normal reruns. Replacing the selection requires an explicit action.
 * Use `MAX_DEMO_PRODUCTS`, default 100 and hard maximum 100. Preserve the
   selected product IDs, names, and URLs, and display which products were
   successfully indexed.
 * Proposed default: sample from the full catalog without filtering for public
   resource availability. Show products with no permitted sources as uncovered,
   not as supported by invented content.
 * Keep request, page, concurrency, timeout, and response-size budgets bounded.
   Honor `Retry-After`; stop on unexpected source behavior.
 
 ## Alternatives considered
 
 * Resample randomly on every run: rejected because the demo and evaluation set
   would not be reproducible.
 * Filter out products without public resources: not selected as the proposed
   default because it can bias the sample and increase discovery traffic. This
   remains an open user decision.
 * Authenticate to access protected pages: rejected; outside MVP scope.
 
 ## Consequences
 
 The initial source behavior must be resolved before Phase 2. The user authorized
 up to 100 additional GET requests for bounded source verification/ingestion;
 that cap does not permit unrestricted crawling. A 100-product manifest does
 not imply that all products have indexed public resources. Accepted source
 terms, host allowlist, and per-run budgets must be recorded before ingestion.
